question: This is the as-found single-line diagram of a building's 480 V switchgear. Utility 2 is out of service, so generator G1 is running and carrying everything it is connected to through closed breakers. Main breaker 52-M1 trips. The operator then closes tie breaker 52-T (it was N.O.); a tie can only restore power if the bus on its other side is energized. No other breaker changes position by itself. G1 cannot carry more than its 950 kW rating, so before closing 52-T the operator sheds loads that lost power: he opens their own load breakers one at a time, largest kW first, stopping as soon as G1's total load after the transfer would be at or below 950 kW. Count only loads that were running before the trip (a load behind an open breaker was not running). How many kW of load that was running before the trip are still without power after the transfer? Answer with an integer number of kW.
references: IEEE Std 141 (Red Book), secondary-selective / main-tie-main low-voltage switchgear single-line diagrams
IEEE Std 315 / ANSI Y32.2 graphic symbols and ANSI/IEEE C37.2 device numbers (52 = AC circuit breaker)

question: This is the as-found single-line diagram of a building's 480 V switchgear. A crew must work on BUS 2B (panel PNL-2B). Bus 2B must be isolated: afterwards there may be no path through closed breakers from any source (utility services, generator G1, or the PV-1 solar inverter) to Bus 2B. Breakers that are already open need no action. Open as few breakers as possible, and do not cut power to any running load that is not fed from Bus 2B. Which breakers must be opened? Answer with the breaker IDs sorted alphabetically, separated by commas.
